about: Pinned toolchain for the installer payload: llvm-mingw, CMake and Ninja, Windows x64. fetch_toolchain.py downloads each entry, checks its SHA-256 and unpacks it under build/installer/toolchain-cache/trees/; assemble_payload.py copies the trees into the payload's toolchain/ and licences/. The Windows Python is staged separately (--python).

components.name: llvm-mingw
components.license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception (clang, lld, compiler-rt, libc++, libunwind); MinGW-w64 headers and CRT: ZPL-2.1 and public-domain parts, some Wine-derived headers LGPL-2.1+ (shipped unmodified as source, text in licenses); winpthreads: MIT and BSD-3-Clause; llvm-mingw build scripts: ISC
components.notice: llvm-mingw {version} by Martin Storsjö (LLVM {llvm}: clang, lld, compiler-rt, libc++, libunwind, Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception; MinGW-w64 headers, CRT and winpthreads under their own permissive terms): the C/C++ compiler the installer bundles to build jsp.exe on the player's machine. jsp.exe links its runtime libraries statically. Licence texts in licenses\llvm-mingw\.

components.name: ffmpeg-headers
components.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later (headers only; the DLLs come from the player's RPCS3)
components.about: Only libavcodec/ and libavutil/ headers go into the payload (assemble_payload.py, which also writes libavutil/avconfig.h for x86-64 Windows), so the toolkit is built with PS3RECOMP_FFMPEG_RUNTIME for the opening movie. The majors (avcodec 63, avutil 61) must match the DLLs of the players' RPCS3 builds; firstrun's check M1 warns when they do not. GitHub's tag zip is not guaranteed byte-identical forever: a hash mismatch here most likely means GitHub re-packed it (check the tag, then refill the hash); it can also be a changed or damaged download.
